Below is a 12‑week progressive couch‑to‑5K running plan tailored for your 24‑year‑old client with exercise‑induced asthma (EIA) who uses a SABA inhaler. It emphasizes gradual progression, thorough warm‑ups, strategies to avoid cold‑air triggers, recovery, and simple nutrition guidance. Before starting, confirm the client has medical clearance and carries/knows how to use their SABA inhaler during all sessions.

Overview and key precautions
- Warm up is essential every session: minimum 8–12 minutes of gradual aerobic warm‑up plus dynamic mobility and progressive intensity (detailed below).
- Use SABA (e.g., 100 µg salbutamol) 10–15 minutes before hard efforts if prescribed to use pre‑exercise, per GP guidance. Confirm his individual plan with the GP.
- Avoid running in very cold, dry air. If <5°C or windy, recommend running indoors on a treadmill or wearing a scarf/buff over mouth and nose to warm and humidify air.
- Start at low intensity. Monitor for cough, chest tightness, wheeze, or excessive breathlessness. If symptoms occur: stop, use inhaler, rest, seek medical help if not resolving.
- Aim goal: continuous 5 km at a comfortable running pace by the end of week 12.
- Frequency: 3 run sessions per week on nonconsecutive days (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri or Tue/Thu/Sat). Optional light cross‑training (CT) on one of the rest days (low intensity: cycling, swimming, brisk walking) only if symptom‑free and approved. Strength and mobility 2x/week short sessions to support running form and injury prevention.
- Progression principle: increase run time gradually ~10–20% week‑to‑week; alternate run/walk intervals early, moving to continuous running.

Warm‑up template (use for every run)
1. Easy walking 3–5 minutes.
2. Dynamic mobility 3–5 minutes: ankle circles, leg swings (front/back + side), hip openers, arm circles.
3. Gentle jog 3–5 minutes, gradually raising pace to an easy conversational jog.
4. 2–4 short pick‑ups (20–30 seconds) at a slightly brisker pace with full recovery (walk/jog 60–90 sec) — only from week 3 onward and only if no EIA symptoms. If using SABA pre‑exercise, schedule inhaler 10–15 min beforehand.

Strength & conditioning (2 sessions per week, 20–25 min)
Do on non‑running days or after easy runs. Focus on core, glutes, hip stability and general strength.
- Glute bridge: 3 x 10–12
- Bodyweight squat (or goblet squat): 3 x 8–12
- Reverse lunges or split squats: 2–3 x 8 each leg
- Single‑leg deadlift (bodyweight or light dumbbell): 2 x 8 each leg
- Plank: 3 x 30–45 sec
- Side plank: 2 x 20–30 sec each side
- Calf raises: 3 x 12–15
Progress load by increasing reps, sets, or light weight every 2–3 weeks.

Recovery and basic nutrition
- Sleep: aim 7–9 hours/night.

A parkrun in Week 8 is a good, practical test — social, flat, and ~5K — but it should be planned carefully given his exercise‑induced asthma and the new tempo/interval work. Here’s a clear plan to make Week 8 parkrun a safe, useful test and training stimulus.

Why Week 8 is reasonable
- By Week 8 he’ll have several weeks of continuous running (30 min runs, tempo work starting) and low‑volume intervals. That builds a base to attempt a 5K.
- A parkrun gives realistic pacing feedback, race rehearsal experience, and motivation.

Precautions and rules
- Get explicit GP confirmation if there is any recent change in asthma control or medication. If he’s been stable and symptom‑free on current meds, proceed with caution.
- Pre‑race: use SABA 10–15 minutes before warm‑up if his GP recommends pre‑exercise inhaler use.
- Avoid parkrun in very cold, dry, or high‑pollen conditions. If outdoors and cold, wear a buff or mask to warm/humidify inhaled air or move to a treadmill alternative (time‑trial).
- Bring inhaler and phone; run with a training partner or inform someone of plans.
- If any asthma symptoms (wheeze, chest tightness, persistent cough) occur pre‑race or during, stop, use inhaler, and follow action plan.

Taper and week plan (Week 8 — parkrun as the test)
Assume standard schedule with tempo day + intervals. Position parkrun as the Saturday morning test; schedule the interval session earlier in the week and make the day before parkrun easy/recovery.

Example Week 8 layout (parkrun Saturday)
- Monday — Easy run 30 min + mobility
- Tuesday — Tempo session: 15–18 min tempo (RPE ~7) after full warm‑up; cool down
- Wednesday — Strength session (light/moderate)
- Thursday — Short interval or sharpener (low volume): Warm‑up, 6 x 30s–45s strides/short pickups at near race pace with full recovery (or 6 x 400 m easy; keep low volume), cool down. Alternatively, skip intervals and do a light easy run if cautious.
- Friday — Rest or very easy 20 min jog/walk + mobility; keep legs fresh and breathing calm
- Saturday — Parkrun (5K test)
- Sunday — Rest or active recovery (walk, gentle cycling) + light mobility

Pre‑parkrun warm‑up (important for asthma and performance)
- 10–15 minutes total before the run:
  1) 5–8 min easy jog/walk and dynamic mobility (leg swings, ankle circles, hip openers)
  2) 3–4 short strides (20–30s) with full recovery between (walk 60–90s)
  3) If using SABA, take 10–15 min before starting the warm‑up so medication is active during the run
- Do not start the parkrun sprinting off the line — begin at an effort you can maintain for a steady 5K. Encourage negative or even pacing: aim for even splits or slight negative split (faster second half) rather than all‑out start.

Pacing strategy for the parkrun
- If he hasn’t done a timed 5K recently, have him treat this as a controlled hard training run, not an all‑out race.
- Aim for a pace that feels “comfortably hard” (RPE ~7–8) — he should be breathing hard but not gasping.
- Practical approach: Run first kilometer at target 5K pace or slightly conservative, then evaluate. If breathing is controlled and asthma symptoms absent, he can push slightly in the middle and final kilometer.
- Use walk breaks if needed — better to complete the parkrun comfortably than to push into an asthma flare.

Post‑parkrun recovery
- Cool down 8–10 min easy walk/jog + gentle stretching and mobility.
- Use rescue inhaler if needed per action plan.
- Refuel: small carb + protein snack within 45–60 minutes (yoghurt & fruit, sandwich, smoothie).
- Saturday post‑parkrun: rest or gentle active recovery. Sunday: rest or very easy 20–30 min recovery run/walk depending on how he feels.

If parkrun goes poorly (asthma symptoms or severe fatigue)
- Stop and treat per asthma plan. If symptoms persist >15–20 minutes despite inhaler, seek medical help.
- Do not force another hard session the following days; allow 48–72 hours of easy activity before resuming progression.
- Consider repeating a lower‑key 5K time trial later (Week 10 or 11) when better prepared.

Logging & learning
- Record parkrun data: time, splits (if possible), perceived exertion, inhaler use, any symptoms, and environmental conditions (temperature, wind, pollen).
- Use this to adjust target paces for the remaining weeks (Weeks 9–12): if parkrun is strong and symptom‑free, push tempo/interval paces up slightly; if symptoms or pacing issues occurred, back off intensity and focus on controlled tempo work.

Monday — Easy + mobility (recovery)
- Run: 20–25 min easy conversational pace (RPE 3–4). Keep breathing calm.
- Mobility: 8–10 min dynamic mobility + light hip/glute activation (glute bridges 2 x 10, band walks 2 x 10 steps).

- Cool down: 8–10 min easy jog + light stretching.

  - Plank: 2 x 30s
  - Calf raises: 2 x 10
- Avoid heavy lifts or high volume. Keep breathing controlled.

- Main: 4–6 x 400 m at goal 5K race pace (or slightly faster) with full recovery (90–120s walk/jog). Keep the efforts controlled — no all‑out sprinting.
- Cool down: 8–10 min easy jog + light stretching
- Alternatively (if he’s cautious about bronchospasm): 6 x 30s near‑race pickups with full recovery.

- AM: Optional very easy 10–15 min shakeout jog (or brisk 10–15 min walk) to loosen up.

Pre‑race checklist (30–60 min before):
- Inhaler: take SABA 10–15 min before warm‑up if GP has advised pre‑exercise use. Confirm dosage instructions with client’s GP.
- Clothing: dress in layers; if cold/dry, use buff/scarf to warm air and avoid bronchial trigger.
- Gear: running shoes, race watch/phone, inhaler, ID, small carbohydrate snack (banana/toast) 30–60 min before if needed.

Warm‑up (recommended 15–20 min)
1) Easy 8–10 min jog/walk + dynamic mobility (leg swings, hip circles).
2) 3–4 strides (20–30s) with full recovery (walk 60–90s) — steady accelerations to near race pace, not sprinting.
3) Final breathing check, mental rehearsal of pacing plan.
Note: If he took SABA, take it 10–15 min before starting the warm‑up.

Pacing & race strategy
- Start conservative: first 800–1000 m at target race pace or slightly conservative (no fast surge). This reduces asthma risk and prevents early lactate spike.
- Mid race (km 1–3): settle into goal 5K pace; monitor breathing. If breathing becomes tight, drop back to steady easy pace or take short walking break to recover.
- Final km: if breathing and legs feel good, increase effort progressively; if any asthma symptoms begin, slow to recover and use inhaler if needed.
- Walk breaks: acceptable — finishing the 5K without provoking an asthma attack is the priority.
- Heart rate/RPE: aim for perceived race effort ~RPE 7.5–8; he should not be gasping for air.

Immediate post‑race
- Cool down: 8–12 min easy walk/jog + very gentle static stretching and mobility.
- Use inhaler if symptoms require, per action plan.
- Refuel: carbohydrate + protein snack within 30–60 min (yoghurt & fruit, sandwich, smoothie).
- Hydrate as required.

Sunday — Recovery & review
- Active recovery: 20–30 min easy walk or very gentle jog, mobility and breathing exercises.
- Review log: record parkrun time, splits, perceived exertion, inhaler use (pre/during/post), any symptoms, environmental conditions (temp, wind, pollen).
- Decide next steps: if parkrun was symptom‑free and successful, progress plan (speed work, more targeted intervals). If issues occurred, prioritise recovery and potentially revisit GP/modify intensity.

Nutrition & hydration notes for race week
- 48 hours pre‑race: normal balanced meals with slightly higher carbohydrate portion at dinner two nights before; avoid unfamiliar or spicy foods.
- Race eve: moderate carb dinner, not overly large. Finish eating 2–3 hours before bedtime if possible.
- Race morning: small carb snack 30–60 min before the warm‑up (banana, toast, small bowl of porridge). Hydrate but avoid overdrinking.
- Caffeine: if he normally uses caffeine before training, a small dose pre‑race can be allowed if it doesn’t provoke asthma or heart palpitations.

Asthma contingency plan (must be clearly understood)
- If symptoms before race: delay start, use SABA, rest and reassess. Only proceed if symptoms clear and breathing feels normal.
- If symptoms during race: stop, use SABA immediately, rest. If symptoms clear in 10–15 min and he feels safe, walk home; if not, call emergency services.
- If repeated increased inhaler use (more than typical), schedule GP review.

Strength taper guidance
- Avoid heavy, high‑volume strength sessions in the 72 hours before race day.
- Wednesday can be light activation only; no heavy squats/deadlifts within 72 hours pre‑race.
- Keep core activation and glute activation short and fresh.

Mental prep & practical tips
- Practice the warm‑up and inhaler routine in a training session earlier in the week so it’s familiar on race day.
- Visualise pacing plan and handling a possible asthma episode calmly.
- Encourage him to log perceived positives (how breathing felt, pacing success) as well as anything to adjust.

Below is the consolidated 12‑week Couch‑to‑5K program for your 24‑year‑old client with exercise‑induced asthma, incorporating:
- progressive run/walk → continuous runs,
- 2× weekly strength program (progressive, running‑specific),
- tempo sessions, interval sessions, and a parkrun 5K test in Week 8,
- a race‑prep (finisher) Week 12 with taper and race‑day routine,
- asthma precautions (warm‑ups, SABA timing, cold‑air guidance), pacing rules, recovery and nutrition notes.

Important safety summary (read first)
- Medical clearance: confirm GP ok with training. Follow GP guidance about pre‑exercise SABA use.
- Warm‑up: always 8–15 min before any sustained or high‑intensity effort (walk/jog, dynamic mobility, build to easy jog, 2–4 short strides/pick‑ups).
- Cold/dry air: avoid if possible; run indoors or wear a buff to warm/humidify inhaled air. Avoid intense efforts in very cold/windy conditions.
- Inhaler: if GP prescribes pre‑exercise use, take SABA 10–15 min before warm‑up for tempo/interval/race sessions. Keep rescue inhaler on person.
- Symptom action: if cough/wheeze/chest tightness/excessive breathlessness occurs — stop, sit, use SABA, wait 10–15 min; seek medical help if not improving.
- Log every session: time/distance, RPE, inhaler use, symptoms, environment.

Structure overview
- 3 run sessions/week: Easy run (recovery), Tempo (quality) OR Interval (quality), Long/easy run (endurance). From Week 8 onward we include both tempo and interval each week; earlier weeks tempo/intros progress conservatively.
- Strength: 2 sessions/week, progressive across 4 phases (Adaptation, Build, Strength, Sharpen). Keep strength sessions on nonconsecutive days and not within 48–72 hours of the parkrun/race heavy day; taper strength in Week 12.
- Progression rule: if a week is too hard, repeat it. Increase pace/volume only if symptom‑free and comfortable.

Warm‑up template (every run; longer before tempo/interval/race)
1) 3–5 min easy walk → 3–5 min easy jog
2) Dynamic mobility 3–5 min: leg swings, hip circles, ankle mobility, arm circles
3) Gradual build to easy jog 2–4 min
4) For quality sessions: 2–4 strides/pick‑ups 20–30s with full recovery
Take SABA 10–15 min before warm‑up if GP recommends pre‑exercise dosing for quality sessions.

Strength program overview (2× week; brief)
- Weeks 1–3 (Adaptation): 20–25 min sessions, bodyweight emphasis.
- Weeks 4–6 (Build): increase load, unilateral work.
- Weeks 7–9 (Strength): heavier single‑leg strength, low‑volume plyometrics.
- Weeks 10–12 (Sharpen): maintain strength, reduce volume; add power work; taper before race.

Details: sets/reps and weekly schedules are shown below.

Pacing guidance
- Easy: conversational, RPE 3–5.
- Brisk/steady: sustainable but challenging, RPE 6–7.
- Tempo: comfortably hard, RPE 6.5–7.5 (sustainable for 12–20 min).
- Intervals: short repeats near 5K pace (intense but controlled), longer repeats at threshold pace slightly slower than 5K pace.
- Use RPE and breathing comfort as primary guides given EIA.

Full 12‑Week plan — week‑by‑week

Week 1 (Adaptation start)
Runs (3)
- Session A (easy/run‑walk): Warm‑up → Run 60s / Walk 90s × 8 → cool down (total ~30 min including warm‑up/cool).
- Session B (easy/run‑walk): Same as A.
- Session C (easy/run‑walk): Same as A.
Strength (2)
- Session S1:
  - Glute bridge 3×12
  - Bodyweight squat 3×10–12
  - Reverse lunge 3×8 each leg
  - Plank 3×30s
  - Single‑leg calf raise 3×10 each
  - Dead bug 2×10 each side
- Session S2:
  - Light RDL (dumbbell) 3×10
  - Step‑ups 3×8 each
  - Hip abduction band 3×12 each
  - Side plank 2×20–30s each side
  - Farmer carry 2×30–45m
Notes: Warm‑up before strength 5–8 min cardio + mobility. Emphasise breathing and avoid breath‑holding.

Week 2
Runs
- A/B/C: Warm‑up → Run 90s / Walk 2 min × 6 → cool down.
Strength
- Same as Week 1. Progress by adding 1–2 reps if easy.

Week 3
Runs
- Session A & C: Warm‑up → Run 2:00 / Walk 1:30 × 7 → cool down.
- Session B: Warm‑up → Run 3:00 / Walk 2:00 × 5 → cool down.
Strength
- Same exercises; progress load slightly or add a set where appropriate.

Week 4 (Introduce longer continuous blocks; short accelerations)
Runs
- A & C: Warm‑up → Run 5:00 / Walk 3:00 × 4 → cool down.
- B: Warm‑up → Run 8:00 / Walk 5:00 × 2 → cool down.
- Add 2–4 short accelerations (20–30s) in warm‑up if symptom‑free.
Strength (Phase 2 start)
- Session S1:
  - Goblet squat 3×8–10
  - Bulgarian split squat 3×8 each
  - Dumbbell RDL 3×8–10
  - Single‑leg calf raises 3×10
  - Plank with shoulder taps 3×30–40s
  - Pallof press 2×10 each side
- Session S2:
  - Step‑ups 3×8 each (heavier)
  - Lateral band walk 3×12 steps each way
  - Single‑leg glute bridge 3×8–10 each
  - Side plank with dips 3×8–10 each
  - Loaded carry 2×40–60m

Week 5 (Start single continuous runs and a steady block)
Runs
- A: Warm‑up → Run 8:00 / Walk 2:00 × 3 → cool down (run total 24 min).
- B (tempo intro): Warm‑up → 10 min easy + 10 min brisk/steady (RPE 6) + 5–10 min easy → cool down.
- C: Warm‑up → Run 20 min continuous easy → cool down.
Strength
- Continue Phase 2; increase load slowly (3×8–10 typical), progress single‑leg work.

Week 6 (Increase continuous run time; add low‑volume plyo introduction)
Runs
- A: Warm‑up → Run 10:00 / Walk 2:00 / Run 10:00 → cool down.
- B: Warm‑up → Run 22–25 min continuous easy → cool down.
- C: Warm‑up → Run 12:00 / Walk 2:00 / Run 12:00 → cool down.
Strength (end Phase 2 → prepare for Phase 3)
- S1:
  - Barbell/goblet squat 3–4×6–8 (moderate)
  - RDL 3×8–10
  - Bulgarian split 3×8 each
  - Calf raises 3×12–15
  - Plank 3×45s
- S2:
  - Single‑leg deadlift 3×6–8 each
  - Step‑up to knee drive 3×8 each
  - Lateral bound or low box hops (controlled) 3×6–8 each (low volume)
  - Pallof press 3×10 each
  - Farmer carry 2×40–60m
Notes: Plyometrics low volume and controlled; remove if triggers asthma.

Week 7 (Progress toward longer continuous running; progressive run)
Runs
- A: Warm‑up → Run 25 min continuous easy → cool down.
- B: Warm‑up → Run 12 min / Walk 1–2 min / Run 12 min → cool down (include a few strides).
- C: Warm‑up → Run 28–30 min continuous easy → cool down.
Strength (Phase 3)
- Heavier strength: Squat 4×6–8, RDL 4×6–8, Bulgarian split 3×8 ea, Calf raises 4×10–12, Plank 3×45–60s, Glute bridge weighted 3×8–10.
- Power: kettlebell swings 3×10 (moderate).

Week 8 — Parkrun test week (first week with both tempo and intervals; parkrun Saturday)
Runs
- Monday (A — easy): 30 min easy + mobility.
- Tuesday (Tempo): Warm‑up 10–15 min incl. strides → 15–18 min continuous tempo (RPE ~7) → cool down 8–10 min.
- Wednesday: Light strength (S1) — moderate activation only.
- Thursday (Sharpener): Short intervals/light speed: Warm‑up 10–12 min → 6×1:00 near 5K pace with 90–120s recovery → cool down.
- Friday: Rest or very easy 20 min shakeout + mobility.
- Saturday: Parkrun 5K test — full warm‑up (10–15 min + 3–4 strides); take SABA 10–15 min before warm‑up if GP recommends. Race strategy: conservative start, even or slight negative splits, stop and use inhaler if symptoms appear. Cool down 8–12 min walk/jog.
- Sunday: Rest/active recovery 20–30 min walk or easy bike + mobility.
Strength
- Two strength sessions in the week (Tue or Wed light and Thu or Fri lighter) but keep loads moderate and avoid heavy lifting within 48–72h of parkrun. Prefer activation and mobility on Wednesday.

Notes for Week 8: Log parkrun time, inhaler use, any symptoms, and environment. Use results to set target paces for Weeks 9–12.

Week 9 (Build intervals & tempo; continue strength)
Runs
- A: Easy 32–35 min.
- B (Intervals): Warm‑up 12 min → 8×45s faster than 5K pace with 60–90s recovery → cool down 8–10 min.
- C: Long easy 35–38 min.
Strength (Phase 3)
- Maintain heavier strength with controlled plyometrics: Squats 4×6–8, RDL 4×6–8, single‑leg deadlift 3×6–8, step‑ups 3×8 ea, calf eccentrics 3×8–10.

Week 10 (Longer threshold work; sharpen speed)
Runs
- A: Easy 36 min.
- B (Threshold/tempo longer): Warm‑up 12–15 min → 3×6:00 at threshold/comfortably hard pace (slightly slower than 5K pace) with 2–3 min recovery → cool down.
- C: Easy 38–40 min.
Strength (Phase 4 — Sharpen)
- Maintain strength but reduce volume slightly: Goblet/front squat 3×6–8, RDL 3×6–8, Bulgarian split 3×6–8, kettlebell swings 3×8–10, single‑leg calf raises 3×8–10. Plyo: short bounds/single‑leg hops 3×4–6.

Week 11 (Race rehearsal; pace sharpening)
Runs
- A: Easy 25–30 min + 4×30s strides (full recovery).
- B (Race rehearsal / intervals): Warm‑up 15 min incl. strides → Option 1: 3–4×1 km at goal 5K pace with 2–3 min jog recovery OR Option 2: 10×400 m at slightly faster than goal 5K pace with 90s recoveries → cool down.
- C: Easy recovery 25–30 min.
Strength
- Light strength, reduce load and volume. No heavy lifts within 72h of test.

Week 12 — Finisher / Race‑day prep week (taper and parkrun/race)
(Place final 5K test on Saturday; this is your race‑prep week.)
Runs & key sessions
- Monday: Easy 20–25 min + mobility (flush legs).
- Tuesday (Short tempo sharpen): Warm‑up 10–12 min → 10–12 min tempo (RPE 6.5–7) or 6×400 m at race pace with full recovery → cool down 8–10 min.
- Wednesday: Light activation strength only (20 min): glute bridges 2×12, single‑leg RDL 2×8 ea, planks 2×30s, calf raises 2×10.
- Thursday (Short sharpener): Warm‑up 12–15 min incl. strides → 6×400 m at 5K pace with 90–120s recovery OR 6×30s near‑race pickups with full recovery → cool down 8–10 min.
- Friday: Rest or very easy 10–15 min shakeout + mobility and breathing drills. Final checks (gear, inhaler, nutrition).
- Saturday: Race day — full pre‑race routine and parkrun/5K target run.
  - Pre‑race: If GP prescribes, take SABA 10–15 min before warm‑up. Snack 30–60 min before if needed.
  - Warm‑up: 10–15 min easy jog + dynamic mobility + 3–4 strides.
  - Race: Start conservative, aim for even splits, use walk breaks if necessary, treat breathing priority first.
  - Cool down: 8–12 min easy walk/jog + mobility.
- Sunday: Recovery: 20–30 min easy walk/jog or bike, mobility, review log.
Strength (Week 12)
- Keep strength very light and short. Avoid heavy lifting in 72 hours before race. Focus on activation and mobility only.

Session notes, pacing & asthma reminders across program
- Warm‑up before every quality session (tempo/intervals/race) must be 10–15 minutes including strides/pick‑ups.
- Use SABA 10–15 min prior to warm‑up for tempo/interval/race if GP advised; keep rescue inhaler accessible for all sessions.
- In cold/dry air, prefer treadmill or mask/buff and reduce intensity.
- If symptoms occur: stop immediately, use SABA, rest; if not improved promptly, seek medical care.
- Adjust progression: repeat any week that feels too hard; don’t progress if EIA symptoms increase.

Nutrition & recovery (overview)
- Sleep: 7–9 hours/night recommended.
- Hydration: drink to thirst; increase in heat.
- Pre‑session: small carb snack 30–90 min before if training fasted is uncomfortable.
- Post‑session: protein + carbs within 1–2 hours.
- Race week: moderate carb increase 48 hours out, normal dinner night before, small carb snack race morning 30–60 min pre‑warm‑up.
- Caffeine: allowed only if he tolerates it and it does not provoke asthma symptoms.

Strength progression quick reference (by phase)
- Phase 1 (W1–3): bodyweight, 3×10–12.
- Phase 2 (W4–6): loaded 3×8–10, single‑leg emphasis.
- Phase 3 (W7–9): heavier 4×6–8, introduce controlled plyo.
- Phase 4 (W10–12): maintain strength, reduce volume, add light power, taper before race.

Example logging fields for each session
- Date, session type, duration, main sets (intervals/tempo), RPE, inhaler use (pre/during/post), symptoms (none/ mild/ moderate), environmental notes (temp/pollen), notes on recovery/soreness.

Adjustments and contingencies
- If parkrun in Week 8 or final test triggers asthma: treat per action plan, rest 48–72 hours, and postpone target to Week 10 or 11 with a modified taper.
- If he improves symptom‑free and the Week 8 parkrun is strong, increase tempo and interval paces moderately (5–10% faster) in Weeks 9–12 as long as inhaler use remains normal.
- If symptoms occur during strength sessions (rare), reduce intensity, split sets, or substitute banded/unilateral alternatives.

Extras I can provide
- Printable weekly sheets (one per week) showing exact sessions.
- Pace conversions (min/km or min/mile) if you give me a baseline 1‑mile, 3 km or 5K time, or his comfortable 30‑min pace.
- A one‑page Race‑Day checklist or a timed warm‑up script he can follow on the morning of the parkrun.

If you want pace targets added, tell me a recent time or estimated pace (e.g., easy run pace for 30 min, or a recent 1 km/1 mile time) and I’ll convert intervals, tempo and race paces to specific min/km or min/mile targets.
